title: Split Array Largest Sum
approach_name: Binary search on maximum segment sum
notes:
Task: Split a nonnegative array into k contiguous nonempty parts while minimizing the largest part sum.
Idea: Binary-search a candidate maximum sum and greedily count the segments required to stay within it.
Invariant: The feasibility check is monotone: if a bound needs at most k segments, every larger bound is feasible too.
Edge cases: The search bounds are the largest element and total sum; nonnegative values are required for the greedy check.
complexity_reason: Each binary-search step scans the array once.

title: Split Array Largest Sum
approach_name: Binary search on maximum segment sum
notes:
Task: Minimize the largest sum among k contiguous segments.
Idea: Binary-search the allowed segment sum and greedily count segments needed under that limit.
Invariant: The feasibility predicate changes monotonically from false to true as the limit increases.
Edge cases: Nonnegative input allows the greedy segment count; the minimum bound is the maximum element.
complexity_reason: Each binary-search iteration makes one linear pass through nums.

title: Fizz Buzz
notes:
Task: Produce the Fizz Buzz sequence from 1 through n.
Idea: Check divisibility by 15, then 3 and 5, otherwise append the decimal number.
Invariant: The output contains the correct representation for every processed integer.
Edge cases: Checking 15 first prevents multiples of both three and five from being labeled only Fizz or Buzz.
complexity_reason: Each number is processed once and all output strings are stored.

title: Fizz Buzz
notes:
Task: Return the Fizz Buzz labels for all integers up to n.
Idea: Apply the combined multiple-of-15 condition before the individual divisibility conditions.
Invariant: Each appended string corresponds to the current integer in ascending order.
Edge cases: Nonmultiples are converted to decimal strings; the result contains exactly n entries.
complexity_reason: The loop emits one string for each integer from 1 through n.

title: Arithmetic Slices
notes:
Task: Count contiguous arithmetic subarrays of length at least three.
Idea: When the current adjacent difference equals the previous one, extend the arithmetic slices ending at the previous index.
Invariant: curr is the number of arithmetic slices ending at the current index.
Edge cases: Arrays shorter than three return zero; any difference break resets curr to zero.
complexity_reason: A single pass updates the number of arithmetic slices ending at each position.

title: Arithmetic Slices
notes:
Task: Count contiguous subarrays of length three or more with equal adjacent differences.
Idea: Extend the count of arithmetic slices ending at the previous position whenever the difference remains equal.
Invariant: curr counts qualifying slices ending at the current index, and total accumulates them.
Edge cases: Fewer than three values produce zero; a changed difference resets curr.
complexity_reason: Each adjacent-difference comparison takes constant time in one pass.

title: Third Maximum Number
notes:
Task: Return the third distinct maximum, falling back to the maximum when fewer than three distinct values exist.
Idea: Maintain up to three distinct values in descending order.
Invariant: first, second, and third are the largest distinct values encountered so far.
Edge cases: Duplicate values do not occupy another slot; if third is absent, return first.
complexity_reason: Only three values are retained and sorting this fixed-size list is constant work.

title: Third Maximum Number
notes:
Task: Find the third largest distinct value, or the largest if fewer than three exist.
Idea: Track the three largest distinct values and ignore duplicates.
Invariant: The three tracked values are the largest distinct values seen in the processed prefix.
Edge cases: Long sentinels avoid confusing Integer.MIN_VALUE with an uninitialized slot.
complexity_reason: The scan maintains only three distinct candidate values.

title: Add Strings
notes:
Task: Add two nonnegative decimal strings without converting the entire strings to integers.
Idea: Add corresponding digits from right to left with a carry.
Invariant: carry and the reversed output represent the sum of the suffixes processed so far.
Edge cases: Unequal lengths are handled by treating missing digits as zero; append a final carry if needed.
complexity_reason: Each input digit is processed once and output digits are stored.

title: Add Strings
notes:
Task: Return the sum of two nonnegative integer strings without parsing them as large integers.
Idea: Add digits from the right, maintaining a carry and collecting result digits in reverse.
Invariant: The carry accounts for overflow from the suffix already processed.
Edge cases: Missing digits contribute zero and a remaining carry is emitted as another digit.
complexity_reason: Each digit is read once and appended to the result builder.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
notes:
Task: Determine whether the array can be split into two subsets with equal sum.
Idea: If the total is even, use a boolean DP to find a subset summing to half the total.
Invariant: dp[s] indicates whether some subset of processed values sums to s.
Edge cases: Odd totals are impossible; iterate sums downward so each number is used at most once.
complexity_reason: Each value updates all reachable sums in descending order.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
notes:
Task: Check whether a subset sums to half of the total array sum.
Idea: Reject odd totals and run one-dimensional 0/1 knapsack DP for target=total/2.
Invariant: dp[s] is true if a subset of values already processed can make sum s.
Edge cases: Descending sum iteration prevents reusing the current value more than once.
complexity_reason: Each array value updates target-sized DP states once.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
notes:
Task: Find cells from which water can flow downhill or level to both oceans.
Idea: Start searches at each ocean's border and move to neighbors of equal or greater height, reversing the water-flow direction.
Invariant: Each visited set contains exactly the cells reachable from that ocean when traversing reverse edges.
Edge cases: Empty matrices return an empty list; intersect the two reachable sets for the answer.
complexity_reason: Each cell is visited at most once per ocean search.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
notes:
Task: Return cells that can reach both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans by non-increasing water flow.
Idea: Run reverse DFS from both sets of borders, moving only to cells at least as high as the current cell.
Invariant: Each visited matrix marks cells that can reach the corresponding ocean.
Edge cases: Empty input returns an empty list; the final result is the intersection of the two visited grids.
complexity_reason: Each cell is visited at most once from each ocean's borders.

title: Battleships in a Board
notes:
Task: Count non-touching horizontal or vertical battleships on a board.
Idea: Count each X only if there is no X immediately above it and no X immediately to its left.
Invariant: Each ship is counted exactly once at its top-left cell.
Edge cases: Empty cells are ignored; the no-touching rule ensures adjacent X cells belong to the same straight ship.
complexity_reason: Each board cell is inspected once and only a counter is stored.

title: Battleships in a Board
notes:
Task: Count straight battleships on a board without modifying it.
Idea: Count each X whose upper and left neighbors are not X.
Invariant: The top-left cell is the unique cell counted for each horizontal or vertical ship.
Edge cases: Boundary checks avoid reading outside the board; ships are guaranteed not to touch diagonally or otherwise.
complexity_reason: The matrix is scanned once with constant extra state.

title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
notes:
Task: Find the largest XOR value obtainable from any two array elements.
Idea: Build the answer bit by bit from most significant to least significant using prefix sets.
Invariant: At each bit, the candidate is retained only if two masked prefixes can XOR to it.
Edge cases: Nonnegative 32-bit integers are assumed; duplicate prefixes are harmless because set membership is sufficient.
complexity_reason: There are 32 bit positions and each iteration builds and checks a set of masked prefixes.

title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
notes:
Task: Maximize the XOR of two values in the input.
Idea: Tentatively set each bit from high to low and test whether two prefixes can realize the candidate.
Invariant: The retained answer is the largest feasible prefix among the bits considered so far.
Edge cases: Prefix sets are sufficient because only the masked high bits affect the candidate bit decision.
complexity_reason: The fixed 32-bit loop builds one set of prefixes per iteration.

title: Reconstruct Original Digits from English
notes:
Task: Recover sorted digits from a string containing shuffled English digit names.
Idea: Count letters and identify digits in an order that uses unique letters first, then subtract those contributions from overlapping counts.
Invariant: Each recovered digit count is fixed by a letter that uniquely identifies that digit among the remaining candidates.
Edge cases: Output digits are emitted in ascending order; the input is assumed to be a concatenation of valid number words.
complexity_reason: The input is counted once and only ten digit counts are stored.

title: Reconstruct Original Digits from English
notes:
Task: Reconstruct all original digits from shuffled English digit-name letters.
Idea: Count letters and solve digit counts in dependency order using unique letters such as z, w, u, x, and g.
Invariant: The counts for digits identified by unique letters are established before dependent counts are calculated.
Edge cases: Emit the digits in ascending numeric order; valid input guarantees nonnegative counts after subtraction.
complexity_reason: The letters are counted in one pass and fixed-size arrays hold the digit frequencies.
